title: Assessing Page Reclamation Mechanisms for Linux
problem: Understanding and quantifying the performance characteristics of Linux page reclamation policies remains challenging. Need for comprehensive analysis of decision-making overhead and reclamation effectiveness.
motivation: Provide guidance for future memory management optimizations by understanding trade-offs in reclamation policies like 2QLRU and MGLRU under various memory constraints.
method: Lightweight profiler to measure decision overhead and reclamation effectiveness of Linux's Two-Queue LRU (2QLRU) and Multi-Generational LRU (MGLRU) policies. Evaluation across seven diverse applications under various memory constraints.
key_novelty: Comprehensive analysis of MGLRU versus 2QLRU with lightweight profiling of both decision overhead and reclamation effectiveness.
contributions: Lightweight profiler for measuring page reclamation decision overhead
Quantification of MGLRU versus 2QLRU performance trade-offs
Analysis across seven diverse applications under memory constraints
workloads: Seven diverse applications under memory constraints
limitations: Abstract does not specify which applications or detail specific overhead/performance numbers. Performance benefits diminish under severe memory constraint but not quantified.
